description:
`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` re-runs itself under `flock "$BUILD_LOCK"`, which passes the lock's file descriptor to the child and every descendant. A descendant that daemonises keeps holding it after the run exits — `sccache` double-forks to PPID 1 and does exactly that — so the lock is never released and the next caller blocks forever against a run that finished long ago.

Observed three times in one session on 2026-08-10; one occurrence blocked a dispatched worker for 9 minutes. The failure is silent: no output, no error, no diagnostic, indistinguishable from a hung or dead process.

The lock path is host-wide (`${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/cargo-ci.lock`) and shared with the sibling gf2 checkout, whose wrapper carries the same defect, so a daemon leaked by either repository wedges the other.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The build lock is released when a run exits, even when that run leaves a daemonised descendant behind.
- [hard] REQ-02: The lock is still held for the whole duration of a run, so host-wide build serialization is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A run that cannot acquire the lock reports what holds it instead of blocking silently, and a bounded wait ends in a named error distinguishable from the wrapped command's own exit status.


## Resolution

Rejected 2026-08-14 as already delivered. Commit `4ce920633` filed this issue and fixed it in
the same change: `flock -o` closes the lock descriptor before exec, so a daemonised descendant
no longer inherits it (REQ-01); the waiting `flock` parent holds the lock for the run's whole
duration (REQ-02); and a non-blocking probe reports the current holders, the wait is bounded,
and `-E 75` separates a lock failure from the wrapped command's own status (REQ-03). The issue
was left ready rather than closed.
title: cargo-ci build lock survives its run through a daemonising child
